bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's Makhana Reaches Greece as APEDA Facilitates 1 MT Export from Purnea
bihar_raw_news.content: Top Stories of the Day Share DD India October 2, 2026 4:43 PM IST Bihar’s Makhana Reaches Greece as APEDA Facilitates 1 MT Export from Purnea Author: DD India The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority, APEDA, has facilitated the export of one metric tonne of popped or Phool Makhana from Purnea in Bihar to Greece. The consignment was flagged off from Purnea, marking another step towards expanding international market access for Bihar’s traditional Makhana and creating opportunities for better returns for farmers through export-oriented value chains. The consignment, sourced by Indo Global Export, Belouri, Purnea, is being exported to Greece through S. S Foods Exports Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi. The shipment will be transported from Mundra Port in India to Piraeus Port in Greece. According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the export has resulted in higher price realisation compared with the prevailing domestic market selling price. This highlights the potential of international markets to create additional value for Makhana producers. The export-led market access is also expected to strengthen linkages between producers and international buyers and create opportunities for improved returns to farmers. India is the world’s leading producer of Makhana, with Bihar accounting for around 80 to 85 per cent of the country’s production. Makhana cultivation in the state covers more than 35,000 hectares across 10 districts. The sector is supported by technical interventions from Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour, and the ICAR-National Research Centre for Makhana, Darbhanga. The flag-off programme was chaired by Bihar Agriculture Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha. APEDA Chairman Abhishek Dev, Director of Horticulture in the Bihar Agriculture Department Abhishek Kumar, senior government officials and other stakeholders associated with the Makhana export value chain were also present. Addressing the gathering, Vijay Kumar Sinha said the export marked an important milestone for Bihar’s Makhana sector as the product continued to gain access to international markets. He said, “The export marks an important milestone for Bihar’s Makhana sector as the product continues to reach international markets.” Sinha said India exported more than 7,000 metric tonnes of Makhana and value-added Makhana products, valued at around USD 22 million, during 2025-26, across more than 20 international destinations. He also said the Government of Bihar was working towards an Agri Export Policy aimed at supporting farmers and improving their incomes through export promotion. The Minister highlighted the development of packhouses to support the Makhana export value chain and commended APEDA for its efforts to expand Makhana exports and improve farmer realisation. The export from Purnea to Greece is part of efforts to connect Bihar’s Makhana producers and exporters with international markets. Makhana, which has a strong traditional and cultural association with Bihar, has emerged as an important product in India’s agricultural export basket. APEDA has been facilitating market linkages and supporting exporters in taking Indian Makhana to international markets. Exports of Makhana are also expanding into European markets, providing opportunities for Indian producers to diversify beyond traditional destinations.

bihar_raw_news.content: SC grants eight weeks to Bihar to remove encroachments from Ganga flood plains in Patna Supreme Court gives Bihar 8 weeks to remove all unauthorized structures and encroachments on Ganga flood plains between Nauzar Ghat and Nurpur Ghat in Patna. By PTI October 2, 2026, 3:49:37 PM IST (Updated) 3 Min Read The Supreme Court has granted eight weeks to the Bihar government to comply with its directions to remove all unauthorised structures and encroachments on the flood plains between Nauzar Ghat and Nurpur Ghat in Patna. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan noted that on July 21, the apex court had granted six weeks to the state to ensure that each and every unauthorised structure and encroachments standing on the Ganga flood plains between Nauzar Ghat and Nurpur Ghat were removed. On September 28, Bihar’s Advocate General S D Sanjay informed the bench that directions issued by the top court were partially complied with. He said the recent natural calamity in Nepal, which led to the level of River Ganga rising, submerged this entire portion and made it difficult for the authorities to proceed further with the removal of encroachments. ”We grant for one last time, eight weeks’ time period to comply with our directions, failing which we shall have to summon the chief secretary of the State of Bihar and other authorities before us and we may also proceed further with contempt,” the bench said. ”After eight weeks, i.e., on the next date of hearing, we want a full compliance report as regards the removal of the encroachments as directed by us. No further time shall be granted,” it said. The top court was hearing a petition challenging a June 2020 order of the National Green Tribunal which had dismissed a plea against illegal constructions and permanent encroachments on the eco-fragile flood plains. In its September 28 order, the bench noted that some intervention applications were filed before it in the matter and these intervenors have said that whatever construction was there, was on their own land and those do not fall within the flood plains. ”In this regard, it may be open for these intervenors to prefer an appropriate representation addressed to the competent authority,” the bench said. The top court said if any representation is preferred by any of the intervenors before it, they shall attach all documents of title over the land, including the authorised sanction and authorisation of building that might have been granted for the purpose of construction. ”In the absence of these documents, no representation shall be looked into,” it said, while disposing of the intervention applications. While hearing the matter in July, the top court had observed that illegal constructions along River Ganga was a matter of concern. bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News PMFME Scheme Clears ₹116 Crore for Maharashtra Food Units Breaking News PMFME Scheme Clears ₹116 Crore for Maharashtra Food Units By Urban Acres October 2, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The PMFME scheme has received approval for ₹116 crore in subsidies for eligible micro food-processing enterprises in Maharashtra, with the funding expected to support projects across the state and strengthen its small-scale processing economy. The approved amount is ₹116 crore, ₹16 lakh and ₹667, with the Centre contributing 60% and the Maharashtra government providing the remaining 40%, according to a report by Loksatta. Maharashtra has established 32,615 projects under the Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises scheme, the report said. The state has been among the leading performers in implementing the scheme since its launch, with food-processing projects spread across several districts. The approval relates to the second instalment for eligible enterprises during the 2026-27 financial year. The central share of the instalment had reportedly been received around 15 days before the approval, while the state government subsequently deposited its 40% contribution. The combined amount has now been approved for distribution to beneficiaries. The funding structure places the release of subsidy support within a shared administrative and financial responsibility between the Union and state governments. While the Centre provides the larger share of the assistance, the state contribution is required before the combined instalment can be distributed to eligible units. The scheme’s implementation has also created a measurable network of small food-processing projects across Maharashtra. These projects are relevant to the state’s district-level economy because they connect local production with processing activity, although the report does not provide a district-wise breakdown of the approved subsidy amount or details of individual beneficiaries. At the national level, Bihar has moved ahead of Maharashtra in the total number of projects established under the scheme, with 34,092 projects, according to the report. Uttar Pradesh has 28,739 projects and Tamil Nadu has 20,407. Maharashtra’s total stands at 32,615 projects. District-level figures show strong representation from Maharashtra among the scheme’s leading locations. Patna in Bihar has the highest number, with 2,745 projects. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar follows with 2,672, while Sangli has 2,575. The report said seven of the 10 highest-performing districts in the country are in Maharashtra. After Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Sangli, the Maharashtra districts identified among the leading performers are Ahilyanagar, Nashik, Satara, Kolhapur and Amravati. Their inclusion indicates that the scheme’s reach is not limited to the state’s largest metropolitan centres and extends across districts with established agricultural and food-production activity. The immediate next step is the distribution of the approved second instalment to eligible enterprises after the Centre and Maharashtra have completed their respective funding contributions. The report does not specify the release date for individual beneficiaries or the subsidy amount assigned to each project. bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar has immense potential to emerge as major investment hub: Nitin Gadkari ANI | Updated: Oct 02, 2026 08:50 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], October 2 (ANI): Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari on Thursday highlighted Bihar 's expanding infrastructure, improved connectivity, skilled human capital and strengthening investment ecosystem, saying the state has immense potential to emerge as a major hub for industry, enterprise and innovation. Gadkari was addressing the Rising Bihar Investor Summit 2026, themed "The Emerging Investment Destination of India", in Patna in the presence of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. The Union Minister underlined the importance of infrastructure and connectivity in supporting Bihar 's economic transformation, saying the state's development of roads and other infrastructure can strengthen access to markets, facilitate industrial activity and create employment opportunities. The Centre has also assured support for infrastructure development in Bihar , with Gadkari highlighting the role of road connectivity in supporting investment and economic growth in the state. The Rising Bihar Investor Summit was organised at Hotel Taj City Centre in Patna and brought together policymakers, investors, industry leaders, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders to discuss the state's investment opportunities and industrial growth roadmap. The summit focused on Bihar 's emerging opportunities across sectors, including industry, energy and power, urban development and housing, roads and connectivity, agriculture and food processing, and IT and IT-enabled services. The event also showcased the state's investment incentives and industrial infrastructure. The Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package 2025 provides fiscal benefits, subsidies and land concessions for eligible projects, while the state has highlighted more than 100 industrial areas as part of its efforts to attract investment. Gadkari said a prosperous and progressive Bihar would have an important role in advancing the vision of a Viksit Bharat, powered by investment, employment, infrastructure and inclusive economic growth. He emphasised that investment-led development, combined with infrastructure expansion and employment generation, could strengthen Bihar 's position in India's broader economic growth story. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, who was present at the summit, invited domestic and international investors to participate in Bihar 's development journey and assured them of government support. The state government has set an ambitious target of attracting investments worth Rs 5 lakh crore by November this year, according to the summit's official website. Choudhary has also highlighted infrastructure development, industrial expansion and employment generation as key priorities, while encouraging industries to establish manufacturing units in Bihar . The summit's investment-focused agenda included sectoral sessions, business-to-government and business-to-business meetings, policy and incentive showcases, industrial infrastructure presentations, startup and innovation initiatives, and district-level investment opportunities. national_raw_news.title: India’s gold rush continues with six gold medals on day 13 at Asian Games 1 hour ago 167
national_raw_news.content: The gold rush continued for India at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance on Day 13, clinching six gold medals in Hockey, Boxing, Wrestling and archery – in a spectacular display of skill, determination and sporting excellence. Indian Women’s Hockey team clinched the gold medal, defeating defending champions China 1-nil in the closely fought final. Lalremsiami Hmarzote scored the decisive lone goal for India, while goalkeeper Savita Punia produced a crucial save from a penalty stroke to preserve the lead and secure the gold medal. The victory marks India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games in 44 years, ending a long wait for the title. The Women’s Hockey team has also secured a direct berth at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Earlier, Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal scripted a remarkable comeback to win the gold medal in the men’s 65-kilogram freestyle event. The 23-year-old Indian produced a stunning fightback in the final, recovering from a 4-9 deficit to defeat Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 and clinch the Asian Games title. With this victory, Sujeet has joined the elite company of Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, becoming the third Indian wrestler to win Asian Games gold in the men’s 65-kilogram category. In Boxing, Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65kg category, defeating Chinese Taipei’s Nien-Chin Chen 3-2 in a split decision in the final. Ankush Panghal clinched the gold medal in the men’s 80-kilogram category, defeating South Korea’s Kim Minseong by a split decision, 4-0, in the final. India’s star woman boxer Lovlina Borgohain also clinched a gold medal in the 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final. It is India’s second gold medal in women’s boxing at the Asian Games, following Mary Kom’s gold in 2014. In archery, the women’s recurve team created history by clinching its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final. India also bagged silver in the mixed recurve team event. Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after going down 3-5 to China in a closely contested final. In Sepaktakraw, India secured the bronze medal in the men’s quadrant event. The Indian team lost 0-2 to Japan in the semi-final but earned a place on the podium. In Sailing, Nethra Kumanan clinched bronze in the women’s dinghy event. The 29-year-old Indian sailor finished third with an overall score of 14 points. With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fifth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 76, including 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.

national_raw_news.content: Ministry mourns demise of three I&B members in Mizoram tragedy | MorungExpress | morungexpress.com Ministry mourns demise of three I&B members in Mizoram tragedy North-East 2nd October 2026 Dimapur, October 2 (MExN): The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has expressed deep grief over the untimely demise of three members of the I&B fraternity who lost their lives in a tragic road accident in Mizoram on October 1. The vehicle carrying the officials plunged into a gorge while they were on official duty. The deceased have been identified as Dr Engam Pame (IIS), Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Imphal; Nampibou Marinmai (IIS), Director (News), Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio, Aizawl; and H Lianvela (MTS), CBC Field Office, Aizawl. Calling the tragedy a profound loss to their respective organisations and the broader public communication sector, the Ministry extended its condolences to the bereaved families. Dr. Engam Pame, 58, a 1984-batch Indian Information Service officer, held an M.A. in International Relations from Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. Over a career spanning more than three decades, he served in Delhi, Imphal, Pune, and Shillong. As Additional Director General of PIB Imphal, he played a key role in strengthening media coordination across the Northeast. He was one of the longest-serving Group A Information Service officers from the region and belonged to the Zeme Naga community of Tamenglong district, Manipur. He is survived by his wife, Ajuna Pame, a son, and a daughter. Nampibou Marinmai served as Director (News) for Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio in Aizawl, and chaired the Inter Media Publicity Coordination Committee (IMPCC). His career included a tenure as Public Relations Officer with the Ministry of Defence. He is survived by his wife, a son, and a daughter. H Lianvela, 52, who joined government service in 1998, served as an MTS official at the CBC Field Office in Aizawl. He is survived by his wife, a daughter, and a grandson. Additionally, Gojendra Dey, a driver with the CBC Field Office in Aizawl, sustained injuries in the accident and is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital, where he is reported to be conscious and under medical care. Liangmai Foundation condoles demises Meanwhile, the Liangmai Foundation, in a condolence message, has expressed profound sorrow over their untimely demise, saying their sudden departure was an immeasurable loss to their bereaved families, colleagues, friends and the wider community they served. It described both Marinmai and Pame as accomplished administrators and committed public servants whose contributions extended beyond their official responsibilities. “They were respected leaders, repositories of knowledge and experience, and dedicated servants of the nation and the people of Northeast India,” the foundation said. The foundation extended its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families, relatives, colleagues and all those who had the privilege of knowing and working with the two officials. The 140th meeting of the Enforcement Task Force (ETF) of CAQM was held on October 1 to review the enforcement status. During the 17-day reporting period, a total of 197 inspections were reported, comprising 10 inspections at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites, 111 inspections in the Industrial Sector and 76 inspections related to Diesel Generator (DG) sets. The industrial sector inspections included 22 inspections conducted as part of a special inspection drive. Based on the inspections, violations were reported in 85 cases, comprising 8 C&D cases, 49 industrial cases and 28 DG-related cases. As per the violations reported by the concerned sectors, various enforcement actions have been proposed. These include closure of 4 C&D projects and 1 industrial unit; sealing of 28 DG sets; issuance of orders/directions for compliance in 17 cases, including 4 DG sets; and Environmental Compensation (EC) in 10 cases. Other proposed actions include issuance of letters to project proponents, re-inspection, forwarding of cases to CPCB/SPCB, advisories and other appropriate follow-up measures. A total of 22 premises were inspected, of which 05 were found compliant and 1 had already been sealed by UPPCB. The actions suggested in the remaining cases include closure of 4 units, sealing of 1 DG set, issuance of orders in 5 cases, imposition of EC in 4 cases, and re-inspection and prosecution in 2 cases, the Ministry said. The status of resumption orders issued after the previous ETF meeting was also reviewed. As of September 30, a total of 9 resumption orders had been issued, comprising 2 industrial units and 7 C&D sites. State-wise, 1 resumption order was issued in Delhi, 3 in Haryana and 5 in Uttar Pradesh. Further, 1 case was transferred to the concerned State Pollution Control Board for final decision, pertaining to an industrial unit in Uttar Pradesh. It was noted that the Flying Squads of the Commission have so far carried out inspections at 28,744 units/projects/entities across NCR. Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh and his Mizoram counterpart Lalduhoma on Friday separately condoled the deaths of the three officials. Aizawl Doordarshan Kendra Director (News) Nampibou Marinmai, Press Information Bureau (PIB) Additional Director General Engam Pame, and a multi-tasking staff (MTS) member of the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) field office in Mizoram, H. Lianvela, were killed when the car in which they were travelling plunged into a deep gorge near Sataek village, about 30 km south of Aizawl, on Thursday night. The driver of the vehicle, Gojendro Dey of Aizwal CBC, sustained severe injuries and was admitted to Zoram Medical College and Hospital (ZMCH) at Falkawn near Aizawl, an official said. According to the official, the four were returning to Aizawl after planting a tree at Sialsuk village in memory of Pame's brother, who had died in an accident, when their vehicle veered off the road and plunged into the gorge after the driver suddenly experienced uneasiness and was unable to move his limbs or open his eyes. The bodies of Nampibou Marinmai and Engam Pame will be sent to their respective hometowns in Manipur on Friday after the autopsy, the official said. The three bodies were brought to ZMCH on Thursday night for postmortem examination, which is scheduled to be conducted on Friday. Leaders of the Mizoram Journalists' Association (MJA) also visited ZMCH on Thursday night to offer condolences and pay homage to the three officials. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Lalduhoma, who is also the president of the ruling Mizo National Front (MNF), and Mizoram Congress President Lal Thanzara on Friday separately condoled the deaths. In a social media post, the Chief Minister wrote: "I am deeply saddened by the tragic and untimely demise of Engam Pamei, PIB Imphal Additional Director General; Nampibou Marinmai, Director (News) of Doordarshan Kendra at Aizawl; and H. national_raw_news.content: Secretary, Department of school education and literacy leads Swachhata Shramdaan under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Secretary, Department of school education and literacy leads Swachhata Shramdaan under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 ANI | Updated: Oct 02, 2026 15:05 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 2 (ANI): The Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, organised a Swachhata Shramdaan at a PM SHRI school in New Delhi as part of the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign. Led by Secretary, DoSEL, T. K. Anil Kumar, the drive was conducted under the aegis of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE and brought together students, teachers, senior officials and officers of the Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan ( KVS ). The cleanliness drive covered the school campus, an adjoining community space and the park in front of the school, bringing the school and surrounding community together in a collective effort to promote cleanliness. The Shramdaan was followed by a tree plantation programme under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam 3.0’. Students participated in the programme to reinforce the message of environmental conservation and sustainable practices. A quiz on the Solid Waste Management Rules was also organised to strengthen students’ understanding of source segregation and responsible waste disposal through interactive learning. The programme highlighted the role of schools in fostering clean, sustainable and environmentally responsible habits among students. It encouraged students to actively contribute to cleanliness and environmental conservation, reinforcing the commitment of the Department of School Education and Literacy towards making Swachhata a part of everyday life and contributing to the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. Senior officials of DoSEL, who actively joined the Shramdaan included Dheeraj Sahu, Additional Secretary; Archana Sharma Awasthi, Additional Secretary; Prachi Pandey, Joint Secretary; Amarpreet Duggal, Joint Secretary, Pankaj K. P. Shreyaskar, Deputy Director General (Statistics); Deepika Jain, Chief Controller of Accounts and Vikas Gupta, Commissioner, Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan, along with the officers of KVS (ANI) Earlier, on October 1, the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare organised a voluntary cleanliness drive or shramdaan under the ‘ Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 ’ campaign near Gate No. 3 of Kartavya Bhavan-1 on Dr Rajendra Prasad Marg in New Delhi . The officials and staff took part in the activity as part of the campaign theme, ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’, reaffirming the emphasis on collective action and public participation in cleanliness initiatives. According to a PIB official, the four were returning to Aizawl after planting a tree at Sialsuk village in memory of Pame's brother, who had died in an accident. The vehicle reportedly veered off the road and plunged into the gorge after Dey suddenly experienced uneasiness and was unable to move his limbs or open his eyes, the official said. The bodies of the three deceased were brought to ZMCH on Thursday night, with postmortem examinations scheduled for Friday. After the autopsy, the bodies of Marinmai and Pame will be transported to their native places in Manipur, the official said. Office-bearers of the Mizoram Journalists' Association visited ZMCH on Thursday to pay their respects and offer condolences to the families of the deceased. Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma, Mizo National Front president Zoramthanga and state Congress president Lal Thanzara also condoled the deaths on Friday. Lalduhoma described the deaths as tragic and untimely and expressed solidarity with the bereaved families. “Their sudden and untimely passing is a profound loss, and I share in the grief of all who mourn them,” the chief minister said. The way waste is handled, communities participate and services are delivered can shape the quality of urban life. The Swachh Bharat Mission has given this everyday transformation a strong foundation across the country. Over time, the focus has moved beyond simply collecting and disposing of waste. Cities are finding ways to recover value from discarded material, encourage responsible habits and make municipal services more efficient. Green practices are also gaining ground as segregation, recycling, reuse and recovery become integral to local systems. Digital monitoring, data-driven systems and better service delivery are helping local bodies to work with greater precision. These efforts are gradually creating urban spaces that balance environmental responsibility with the needs of everyday life. Cities Leading the Way in Sustainable Urban Transformation Across different regions, cities are demonstrating how local solutions can translate into meaningful environmental outcomes. Their experiences show that sustainable urban transformation can take many forms. These include converting dumping grounds into integrated waste management facilities and promoting zero-waste practices. Technology is also improving everyday sanitation services and strengthening urban systems. The following stories highlight these diverse approaches. A Greener Goa: Turning Waste into Energy Located in the valleys of Saligao, Goa, the Integrated Waste Management Facility Center promotes environmental sustainability. Spread across 113,000 square metres , it is operated by the Goa Waste Management Corporation (GWMC). The facility was formerly used as a garbage dump. It has now been transformed into an integrated, eco-friendly waste management hub for Goa. The center manages 250 metric tons of wet and dry waste every day. At this plant, organic matter is separated from waste and converted into biogas, which helps generate electricity . This energy supports the needs of the local community by alleviating power shortages in the area. Wet waste from restaurants is converted into valuable bioproducts, including methane-rich biogas. Recyclable materials are recovered from 100 metric tons of dry waste processed at the facility. The remaining dry waste is sent to cement factories for co-processing. Additionally, 1.32 kilowatts of electricity is generated from wet waste at the facility. This electricity powers 35 units, with half supplied to the Goa Electricity Department. The plant also generates 7–8 tons of compost daily. Local panchayats use this compost for gardening and reforestation projects. The integrated solid waste management facility is strengthening Goa’s waste management system, processing approximately one-third of the state's total waste .
